title: Landform type — one row of content/world/lexicon/landforms.json. SHAPE ONLY: the census (170/178/8/23/40) is asserted by scripts/tests/landform-lexicon.test.mjs and by G-LANDFORM, never duplicated here — a bound written into a schema turns its gate rule into dead code.

biomes.title: Free-form in SHAPE (a schema bound would duplicate a gate rule), but CLOSED in fact against scripts/lib/spine.mjs's BIOMES, which Task 5 widened from 12 to 20 precisely so this join could hold. The 170 rows name 19 distinct strings and all 19 are members; the 8 Task 5 added (badland desert karst lake lava reef scree tundra) are exercised by 93 rows. `built` is the one BIOMES member no row names — it is a composition biome, not a landform biome. The join is enforced twice: G-LANDFORM fails on any row naming a non-member (any content root), and world-budget.test.mjs pins both the join and the fact that the added 8 are used.

absentBecause.title: null = this type is INTENDED to be placed in content/world/fabric/; a string = deliberately absent, and the string is the reason. G-LANDFORM enforces the declaration in one direction only: declared-yet-placed is a failure (a stated reason contradicted by a real instance). Unplaced-with-null is a WARNING, never a failure — as a failure it demanded 170/170 coverage and made budgets.json's typeCoverageFloor unreachable. See content/world/budgets.json landformsWhy.
